alignments.note: Article before the name Ἰησοῦς; the ASV writes no determiner for it (rule 23).
Connective δέ rendered by the verse-opening And.
Name on its own English word, split from its article under rule 26.
Circumstantial participle converted to a finite verb; it keeps only uttered, the supplied juncture and going to the following finite verb under rule 88.
Both φωνήν and μεγάλην are anarthrous, so the supplied determiner a belongs to the noun and the phrase is discontinuous under rules 58 and 15.
Attributive adjective on its own English word, the determiner having gone to the noun under rule 58.

The supplied juncture and is a rule 7/29 helper on the finite verb it introduces (rule 88). Head on ghost as the meaning-bearing complement of the support verb gave up under rule 17; heading on gave remains defensible, but gave carries no part of ἐκπνέω's own sense.

review_notes: s001 left unrepresented per rule 23 (article before a name); a reference comparison reporting it is not a correction.
The whole of t007–t011 is kept on ἐξέπνευσεν rather than splitting the juncture off as added, since a participle-to-finite conversion stands in the same clause (rules 88, 98).
